To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the students who took online courses in French as a foreign language at the university level were able to: - communicate in the target language, - interact with native speakers of French, - develop a positive attitude towards French and French culture, - develop a better understanding of their own culture, and - develop a positive intercultural attitude.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a number of issues: the nature of the relationship between culture, intercultural competence, and language learning, the nature and scope of the concept of interculturality, and how these issues can inform the development of a new model of language learning, one in which the intercultural dimension is central.
the development of the concept of intercultural competence and with the development of a methodological framework for its operationalization in a virtual learning environment.
a number of issues that are important to the development of a theory of second language learning, and to the design and evaluation of second language learning programs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study has provided evidence that the use of the internet as an educational tool in the teaching of English as a second language is beneficial.
the use of the online platform in the teaching of French as foreign language at the University level is an important step towards the achievement of intercultural competences.
the use of the Internet in the EFL classroom is a double-edged sword.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in how culture affects teaching, how teaching is influenced by the culture of the students and how the culture of the teachers affects the teaching of culture.
the use of the Internet as an educational medium has been a success in our experience.
we have developed a new approach for teaching French as a foreign language (FFL), which we have called the intercultural approach to French as a Foreign Language.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cultural dimension of teaching is not only an issue of content, but also of teaching methods and learning strategies, and that the cultural dimension is a crucial element of the teaching and learning processes.
the intercultural dimension of a French course with university objectives is an essential part of the course.
the intercultural dimension of teaching French at a distance is not only a theoretical issue.
